helpful: The provisioned document texts were decisive here: full petition and BIO text made the acquiescence posture and the merits arguments directly readable, no retrieval needed.
The statpack merits table's per-Term disturbed rates with the excluded-count guard made the baseline pooling mechanical.
gaps: CourtListener MCP returned HTTP 429 (1400/day quota already exhausted) on the first call of this cell; a per-cell or per-run quota reservation, or surfacing remaining quota to the agent, would avoid burning a call to discover exhaustion.

No committed cut exists for merits disturbed rates conditioned on cert posture (e.g. respondent-acquiesced grants vs. contested grants); I had to apply an unquantified judgment haircut for the acquiescence signal.
fedcourts query's --citation filter is too sparse on SCOTUS rows to surface doctrinal neighbors; a topic/subject filter on SCOTUS rows would have found the Court's prior EAJA cases.
notes: Merits grant-moment cell, forward mode. Prediction rests on provisioned inputs plus the committed statpack after graceful degradation of both live retrieval surfaces.
